phenotype_details.name: Moderate Paraoxonase Activity
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Intermediate antioxidant protection from PON1; balanced approach to dietary fat quality recommended

dietary_recommendation.notes: PON1 protects LDL from oxidation. Lower activity increases vulnerability to oxidised lipids. Polyphenol-rich foods (berries, green tea, pomegranate) upregulate PON1 expression regardless of genotype.

fast.name: High Paraoxonase Activity
fast.dietary_impact: Robust antioxidant protection via PON1. Efficient hydrolysis of oxidised lipids on LDL particles. Standard dietary fat guidelines apply; natural resilience to moderate oxidised fat exposure.

intermediate.name: Moderate Paraoxonase Activity
intermediate.dietary_impact: Intermediate PON1-mediated antioxidant capacity. Emphasise fresh, minimally processed fat sources and antioxidant-rich foods (berries, leafy greens, green tea) to support lipid protection.

slow.name: Low Paraoxonase Activity
slow.dietary_impact: Reduced PON1 enzymatic activity increases sensitivity to oxidised and processed fats. Prioritise antioxidant-rich foods alongside dietary fats — extra virgin olive oil over refined oils, raw nuts over roasted, and abundant polyphenol sources to upregulate PON1 expression.

pon1_antioxidant.notes: PON1 rs662 G allele (192R) has higher paraoxonase activity but lower lactonase/arylesterase activity — the net dietary effect depends on substrate. rs854560 T allele (55M) reduces serum PON1 concentration. Combined haplotype determines functional phenotype. African populations have highest G allele frequency (~65-74%), East Asians ~65%, Europeans ~28%, South Asians ~37%.

phenotype_details.name: Intermediate Carb Sensitivity
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Moderate GCKR-mediated carbohydrate sensitivity; benefits from balanced glycaemic load management

dietary_recommendation.notes: GCKR P446L affects hepatic glucokinase regulation. T allele carriers have lower fasting glucose but higher triglycerides — a paradoxical metabolic trade-off favouring carbohydrate tolerance at the cost of lipid metabolism.

normal.name: Standard Carbohydrate Processing
normal.dietary_impact: Normal GCKR-mediated glucokinase regulation. Standard carbohydrate tolerance with typical hepatic glucose uptake. Balanced macronutrient distribution appropriate.

intermediate.name: Intermediate Carb Sensitivity
intermediate.dietary_impact: Moderate GCKR variant frequency. Some enhancement of hepatic glucose uptake but mildly elevated triglyceride tendency. Favour complex carbohydrates over simple sugars; monitor triglycerides with high-carb diets.

sensitive.name: Enhanced Carb-Triglyceride Sensitivity
sensitive.dietary_impact: Higher GCKR 446L frequency — enhanced hepatic glucose uptake but elevated triglyceride response to carbohydrate-rich meals. Prioritise low-glycaemic-index carbohydrates, pair carbs with protein/fat, and limit fructose. Traditional diets based on whole grains and legumes are metabolically well-matched.

gckr_carb_sensitivity.notes: rs1260326 T allele (P446L) is one of the strongest GWAS signals for fasting triglycerides. Paradoxically lowers fasting glucose while raising triglycerides. Global T allele frequency ~29-41% depending on population. Highest in East Asians (~46%) and Europeans (~40%), lower in Africans (~12%).

phenotype_details.name: Balanced Macronutrient Preference
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Intermediate FGF21 signalling; moderate carbohydrate/sweet preference tendency

recommended_approach: mindful eating to recognise carb cravings
dietary_recommendation.notes: FGF21 is a hepatokine that signals carbohydrate/sugar intake status. rs838133 A allele associates with higher carbohydrate and sugar intake, lower protein and fat intake. Understanding genetic preference can help with conscious dietary choices.

fat_preferring.name: Fat-Preferring Metabolism
fat_preferring.dietary_impact: Lower FGF21-driven carbohydrate craving. Natural tendency toward higher fat, lower sugar intake. Well-suited to moderate-fat dietary patterns with adequate complex carbohydrates for energy balance.

balanced.name: Balanced Macronutrient Preference
balanced.dietary_impact: Intermediate FGF21 carbohydrate signalling. Moderate sweet preference. Balanced macronutrient distribution works well; be mindful of sugar intake without strict restriction.

carb_preferring.name: Carbohydrate-Preferring Metabolism
carb_preferring.dietary_impact: Higher FGF21-driven carbohydrate and sweet preference. Genetic tendency toward higher sugar and carb intake. Channel preference toward complex carbohydrates, fruits, and whole grains rather than refined sugars. Ensure adequate protein at each meal to balance macronutrient intake.

fgf21_carb_preference.notes: rs838133 A allele is the major allele globally (~55-60%). Associated with ~5-10% higher carbohydrate intake and higher sweet taste preference per allele. Also associated with higher alcohol intake. FGF21 acts as a macronutrient-specific endocrine signal from liver to brain.

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Triglyceride Response
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Intermediate triglyceride response to dietary fat; benefits from mindful fat quality and quantity management

dietary_recommendation.notes: APOA5 is a key regulator of plasma triglycerides. The -1131C allele reduces APOA5 transcription, impairing triglyceride clearance. Effect is amplified by high-fat meals and alcohol.

normal.name: Normal Triglyceride Fat Response
normal.dietary_impact: Efficient APOA5-mediated triglyceride clearance. Standard dietary fat tolerance. Balanced fat intake with emphasis on quality sources is appropriate.

intermediate.name: Intermediate Triglyceride Sensitivity
intermediate.dietary_impact: Moderate APOA5 promoter variant frequency. Some elevation in postprandial triglycerides with high-fat meals. Favour omega-3-rich fats, moderate total fat intake, and limit alcohol to support triglyceride clearance.

elevated.name: Elevated Triglyceride Response
elevated.dietary_impact: Higher APOA5 -1131C frequency impairs triglyceride metabolism. Elevated postprandial lipemia after fatty meals. Strictly prioritise omega-3 fatty acids over saturated fats, limit alcohol, avoid combining high-fat and high-carb meals, and consider smaller, more frequent meals to reduce triglyceride spikes.

apoa5_triglycerides.notes: rs662799 C allele raises plasma triglycerides by ~15-20% per allele. Dramatic population variation: ~34% in East Asians, ~28% in South Asians, ~8% in Europeans, ~12% in Africans. Gene-diet interaction well-documented — C carriers benefit most from omega-3 supplementation and fat restriction.

slc6a4_serotonin.variant: 5-HTTLPR (L/S alleles; rs25531 modifies L allele function)

phenotype_details.name: Intermediate Serotonin Transport
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Moderate serotonin transporter efficiency; balanced tryptophan intake and regular meal timing support stable mood and appetite

dietary_recommendation.carbohydrate_approach: complex carbs to support serotonin synthesis
dietary_recommendation.meal_timing_note: Regular meals important — serotonin fluctuations affect appetite and mood
dietary_recommendation.notes: SLC6A4 5-HTTLPR S allele reduces serotonin reuptake transporter expression by ~50%. S/S individuals have lowest synaptic serotonin clearance. Dietary tryptophan (serotonin precursor) and carbohydrate-facilitated tryptophan transport become more important with reduced transporter function.

efficient.name: Efficient Serotonin Transport
efficient.dietary_impact: Robust serotonin transporter expression (L/L genotype). Efficient synaptic serotonin regulation supports stable mood-food relationships. Standard tryptophan-rich diet adequate.

intermediate.name: Intermediate Serotonin Transport
intermediate.dietary_impact: One copy of S allele (L/S genotype). Moderate serotonin transporter expression. Regular tryptophan-rich foods (eggs, turkey, salmon, seeds) and consistent meal timing help maintain stable serotonin signalling and reduce stress-related eating.

reduced.name: Reduced Serotonin Transport
reduced.dietary_impact: Two copies of S allele (S/S genotype). Significantly reduced serotonin transporter density. Prioritise daily tryptophan-rich foods, pair with complex carbohydrates to enhance brain tryptophan uptake, maintain regular meal timing, and consider B6/folate adequacy for serotonin synthesis. Stress-eating tendency may be higher — structured meals help.

slc6a4_serotonin.notes: 5-HTTLPR is a 43-bp insertion/deletion polymorphism in the SLC6A4 promoter. The S (short) allele has ~50% lower transcriptional efficiency. East Asian populations have highest S allele frequency (~70-80%), African ~25-35%, European ~42-45%. rs25531 G allele converts functional L to 'Lg' (functionally equivalent to S). Gene × environment interaction is well-documented for stress, mood, and eating behaviour.

phenotype_details.name: Standard Histamine Clearance
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Normal HNMT-mediated intracellular histamine metabolism; standard dietary histamine tolerance

recommended_approach: fresh foods over aged/fermented when symptomatic
dietary_recommendation.notes: HNMT methylates intracellular histamine. Thr105Ile reduces enzyme stability and activity by ~50%. Unlike DAO (which handles extracellular/gut histamine), HNMT is the primary histamine-degrading enzyme in the brain and bronchi.

normal.name: Normal Histamine Clearance (HNMT)
normal.dietary_impact: Efficient intracellular histamine N-methyltransferase activity. Standard tolerance for histamine-containing foods. No specific dietary restrictions needed for histamine management.

intermediate.name: Intermediate Histamine Clearance
intermediate.dietary_impact: Moderate HNMT variant frequency. Some reduction in intracellular histamine clearance capacity. Be mindful of cumulative histamine load — spacing high-histamine meals and emphasising fresh foods can help manage tolerance.

reduced.name: Reduced Histamine Clearance
reduced.dietary_impact: Higher frequency of HNMT 105Ile variant reduces intracellular histamine metabolism by ~50%. Increased sensitivity to histamine-rich foods (aged cheese, fermented products, cured meats, leftover proteins). Prioritise fresh foods, consider low-histamine diet during symptom flares, and support methylation with adequate B vitamins.

hnmt_histamine.notes: rs1801105 T allele (Ile105) frequency is relatively low globally: ~10-14% in Europeans, ~5-8% in East Asians, ~7-10% in Africans, ~8-12% in South Asians. HNMT is distinct from DAO (diamine oxidase) — HNMT handles intracellular histamine via methylation, while DAO handles extracellular/dietary histamine via oxidative deamination.

cyp4f2_vitamin_e.risk_allele: A (433M — but this is 'beneficial' for vitamin E status)

phenotype_details.name: Standard Vitamin E Catabolism
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Normal CYP4F2-mediated vitamin E and K metabolism; standard dietary requirements

dietary_recommendation.vitamin_k_interaction: CYP4F2 also catabolises vitamin K1 — reduced catabolism means lower warfarin dose requirement
dietary_recommendation.notes: CYP4F2 V433M reduces omega-hydroxylation of both vitamin E (tocopherols) and vitamin K1. The M allele results in higher circulating vitamin E and K levels due to slower catabolism. Clinically relevant for warfarin dosing.

normal.name: Normal Vitamin E Catabolism
normal.dietary_impact: Standard CYP4F2 enzyme activity. Normal rates of vitamin E and K catabolism. Standard dietary vitamin E intake from nuts, seeds, and oils is adequate.

intermediate.name: Intermediate Vitamin E Metabolism
intermediate.dietary_impact: Moderate CYP4F2 433M variant frequency. Mildly reduced vitamin E/K catabolism resulting in somewhat higher circulating levels. Standard dietary intake sufficient; supplementation less likely to be needed.

reduced_catabolism.name: Reduced Vitamin E/K Catabolism
reduced_catabolism.dietary_impact: Higher CYP4F2 433M frequency significantly reduces vitamin E and K breakdown. Higher baseline circulating vitamin E — supplementation may be unnecessary or require lower doses. Important for warfarin users: reduced vitamin K catabolism means lower warfarin dose requirements.

cyp4f2_vitamin_e.notes: rs2108622 A allele (V433M) frequency: ~24-29% in Europeans, ~20-24% in East Asians, ~8-12% in Africans, ~20-25% in South Asians, ~27% in Middle Eastern. M allele reduces CYP4F2 protein levels by ~50%. Pharmacogenomic significance: CPIC guideline recommends CYP4F2 genotyping for warfarin dosing.

apoc3_omega3_response.risk_allele: C2 haplotype (variant alleles at both promoter sites)

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Omega-3 Response
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Intermediate omega-3 fatty acid responsiveness; benefits from consistent marine omega-3 intake

dietary_recommendation.target_intake: aim for 2-3 servings fatty fish per week
dietary_recommendation.notes: APOC3 C2 haplotype reduces the triglyceride-lowering response to omega-3 supplementation. C1/C1 homozygotes show strongest triglyceride reduction with fish oil. C2 carriers may need higher omega-3 doses or additional interventions.

responsive.name: Strong Omega-3 Response
responsive.dietary_impact: Robust triglyceride-lowering response to omega-3 fatty acids via efficient APOC3 regulation. Fish oil and marine omega-3s effectively reduce triglycerides. 2-3 servings of fatty fish per week or standard supplementation highly effective.

intermediate.name: Intermediate Omega-3 Response
intermediate.dietary_impact: Moderate APOC3 C2 haplotype frequency. Partial triglyceride-lowering response to omega-3s. Consistent omega-3 intake recommended — aim for fatty fish 3+ times per week and consider supplementation for optimal triglyceride management.

blunted.name: Blunted Omega-3 Response
blunted.dietary_impact: Higher APOC3 C2 haplotype frequency reduces triglyceride-lowering response to omega-3 supplementation. Higher omega-3 doses may be needed, and combination approaches (omega-3 plus reduced refined carbs plus exercise) are more effective than omega-3 alone for triglyceride management.

apoc3_omega3_response.notes: APOC3 -482C>T (rs2854116) and -455T>C (rs2854117) form a functional haplotype affecting insulin response element activity. The C2 haplotype (variant alleles) increases APOC3 expression, raising triglycerides and blunting omega-3 response. C2 frequency: ~30-40% in South Asians (highest), ~25-35% in Europeans, ~15-25% in East Asians, ~20-30% in Africans.

cyp19a1_phytoestrogen.risk_allele: context-dependent (T allele of rs10046 increases aromatase)

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Aromatase Activity
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Intermediate phytoestrogen metabolism; moderate response to dietary isoflavones and lignans

dietary_recommendation.notes: CYP19A1 encodes aromatase, which converts androgens to estrogens and also metabolises phytoestrogens. Higher aromatase activity means faster phytoestrogen metabolism but also higher endogenous estrogen production. Dietary phytoestrogens may have different effects depending on aromatase status.

low_aromatase.name: Lower Aromatase Activity
low_aromatase.dietary_impact: Reduced CYP19A1 aromatase expression. Slower phytoestrogen metabolism means dietary phytoestrogens (soy, flax) may have more prolonged effects. Lower endogenous estrogen production. Phytoestrogen-rich foods may provide compensatory estrogenic activity, particularly beneficial post-menopause.

moderate.name: Moderate Aromatase Activity
moderate.dietary_impact: Intermediate aromatase expression. Balanced phytoestrogen metabolism. Standard dietary phytoestrogen intake from traditional sources (soy, legumes, flaxseed) well-tolerated and beneficial.

high_aromatase.name: Higher Aromatase Activity
high_aromatase.dietary_impact: Elevated CYP19A1 aromatase expression. Rapid phytoestrogen metabolism and higher endogenous estrogen production. High phytoestrogen intake may have less impact due to faster clearance. Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, kale) support healthy estrogen metabolism via alternative pathways.

cyp19a1_phytoestrogen.notes: rs10046 T allele increases CYP19A1 expression and aromatase activity. Frequency: ~48-52% in Europeans, ~30-35% in East Asians, ~35-40% in Africans, ~42-48% in South Asians. rs4646 is in partial LD with rs10046. CYP19A1 variants are clinically significant for breast cancer aromatase inhibitor response and bone mineral density.
